# Export Archicad element properties to Excel with *Python.*

Tapir comes with a script for it: Property Value Exporter writes the values of the properties you choose into an Excel workbook or a CSV file, one row per element, without an Interactive Schedule. Property Value Importer reads the edited file back.

## Open the script

Install the Tapir Add-On with the Tapir Installer, as [Get started](https://archicad-api.com/start/#install) shows, and start Archicad with a project open. Choose *Tapir Palette* from the *Tapir* menu.

Property Value Exporter is a built-in script, so it is in the palette from the start: pick *PropertyValueExporter* in the palette's list and click *Run Script*. It reads every property of the project and opens its window. It is also on the Scripts page as [Property Value Exporter](https://archicad-api.com/scripts/?s=property-value-exporter).

## Choose the elements and the properties

  - Under *Elements*, choose *Selection*, *Current story* or *Whole project*, and if you want *Only elements on visible layers*.
  - Tick the element types to export. *All types* and *No types* tick or untick every one.
  - Under *Properties*, find properties with *Search* and move them to the *Exported* list with *Add →* or a double-click. *Up* and *Down* set the order of the columns; *← Remove* takes one out again.
  - Tick *Precise numbers* to export numbers in SI units (m, m², m³, degrees) instead of the values as Archicad displays them. Leave it off for a file you want to read back in.

## Export

Press *Export...* and choose the file. Its default name is `Property values <date> <time>.xlsx`; give it a `.csv` name for a CSV file. Nothing in the project changes.

The file has the columns *GUID*, *Element ID*, *Type* and *Story*, then one column per property, headed `<group>: <name>`. Rows are sorted by type, story from the bottom up and Element ID. A property an element does not have gives an empty cell. The file cannot be written while it is open in Excel.

## Bring the edited values back

Edit the values in Excel, then run [Property Value Importer](https://archicad-api.com/scripts/?s=property-value-importer). It is not built in: download it from the Scripts page into a folder of your own, with copies of the `utilities/` and `aclib/` folders of [`builtin-scripts/`](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/tree/main/builtin-scripts) next to it. Add that folder to `localFolders` in `Documents/Tapir/config.json`, as [Get started](https://archicad-api.com/start/#marketplace) shows, then choose *Reload scripts...* at the bottom of the palette's script list.

  - Press *Open file...* and choose the `.xlsx` or `.csv` file. A row is matched to its element by its GUID, or by its Element ID when it has no GUID.
  - The list shows each value that would change as *Current* → *New*, and in red what cannot be written, with the reason. An empty cell leaves the value as it is.
  - Press *Write to Archicad* and confirm. The values are written in one Undo step, and the *Result* column says *Written* or why a value was refused, for example because the property is read-only for that element.

## The commands *behind it.*

Both scripts are Python that sends Tapir commands to Archicad. The exporter lists the properties with [`GetAllProperties`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetAllProperties), finds the elements with [`GetElementsByType`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetElementsByType) or [`GetSelectedElements`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetSelectedElements), reads their ID, type and story with [`GetDetailsOfElements`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetDetailsOfElements) and their values with [`GetPropertyValuesOfElements`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetPropertyValuesOfElements). The importer writes the values with [`SetPropertyValuesOfElements`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetPropertyValuesOfElements).

Their code is [`builtin-scripts/PropertyValueExporter.py`](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/PropertyValueExporter.py) and [`marketplace/property-value-importer/PropertyValueImporter.py`](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/marketplace/property-value-importer/PropertyValueImporter.py). Both work in Archicad 25 to 30 with Tapir 1.8.0 or later.
